title: fix: safety block error body; remove unused NSFW output check
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fix: a request blocked by the Bedrock safety filter (`safe=sexual` etc.) now returns `code: content_blocked` and the triggered categories. Before, the shared error handler replaced the custom body with a generic 400.
- Removes the old provider-flag output check (`isMature`/`isChild` → 400 "NSFW content detected", plus a 5 s sleep) and the flags from every image model. Only Azure Flux Kontext and fal Z-Image ever set them, and prod `generation_event_v2` has 0 hits in 60 days.
- Keeps the image `safe` boolean: it still drives the Gemini safety threshold and the Azure prompt check.
- Updates `docs/safety.md` and the block test, which now runs through the production error handler (it fails on main).

| Blocked request | Body |
|---|---|
| Before | `code: BAD_REQUEST`, "Something was wrong with the input data…" |
| After | `code: content_blocked`, "Request blocked by safety filter: sexual" |

Conflicts: the model-retirement branch deletes `novaCanvasModel.ts`, and #15236 adds `isMature: false` lines that need dropping after this merges.

gist.headline: The safety gate speaks plainly
gist.blurb: When an image request meets a safety filter, the hive now returns the actual note instead of a generic shrug. The old, mostly ornamental provider-flag check has also been composted.
gist.summary: Blocked Bedrock image requests using `safe=sexual` and related filters now preserve a `content_blocked` response with the triggered safety categories through the production error handler, while the unused `isMature`/`isChild` output-flag check and its 5-second delay were removed.
gist.impact: API clients can now reliably distinguish safety-filtered requests from generic bad input and receive messages such as `Request blocked by safety filter: sexual`; the existing `safe` boolean continues to control Gemini thresholds and Azure prompt checks.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden API safety gate is correctly stamping a clear `CONTENT BLOCKED` notice on a request leaf, rather than sending it into a vague error fog. Polli, wearing a tiny librarian-style safety visor, calmly reads the labeled notice while a small CRT robot holds a tidy error-response printout; flowering code-plants and a retired dusty flag sign represent removal of the unused provider output flags.
